effects: Exactly `assets` USDT moves from the signer (msg.sender) to the vault (enter: SafeERC20Lib.safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)).
previewDeposit(assets) gtusdtf shares are minted to onBehalf (createShares(onBehalf, shares)). The share count comes from the vault's price after accrueInterest, and no minimum is enforced.
The deposited USDT may be moved on to the liquidity adapter (allocateInternal). That changes no balance of the signer.
formats.shown: Deposit 1 USDT for <onBehalf>, with the share ticker gtusdtf and the address that gets the shares.

findings.title: deposit: the number of gtusdtf shares received is not shown and has no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets);` uses storage totals. The descriptor shows only the constant `Share ticker` = gtusdtf. In case 0 the signer received 996764339939593104 gtusdtf (about 0.9968), and the screen gives no amount.
findings.fix: No calldata value carries it. The share count would need a computed field or a minimum-shares parameter.

cases.notes: The USDT out (1 USDT to the vault) is shown exactly. The gtusdtf in has the right asset and recipient, but the amount (0.9968 shares) is not shown because the vault decides it.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: previewWithdraw(assets) gtusdtf shares (rounded up) are burned from onBehalf (deleteShares). The vault price decides the count.
When msg.sender != onBehalf, the onBehalf → msg.sender share allowance drops by the burned shares.
Exactly `assets` USDT goes from the vault to receiver (safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets)).
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly 0.5 USDT to <receiver>, with the owner whose shares are used.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of gtusdtf shares burned from the owner is not shown and has no cap.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets);` then exit → deleteShares(onBehalf, shares). In case 2 the signer lost 498381919057564852 gtusdtf, and no field names the shares or their amount.
findings.fix: No calldata value carries it. A label such as 'Shares burned from' on the onBehalf field would at least name the asset that leaves.

cases.notes: The 0.5 USDT in to the signer is shown exactly. The gtusdtf burned (0.498 shares) is shown only as 'Owner', with no asset or amount. The reader guessed 'vault share worth about 0.5 USDT'.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Exactly `shares` gtusdtf are burned from onBehalf (deleteShares).
When msg.sender != onBehalf, the onBehalf → msg.sender share allowance drops by `shares`.
previewRedeem(shares) USDT goes from the vault to receiver. The vault price decides the amount, and no minimum is enforced.
formats.shown: Redeem 7178.31 gtusdtf to <receiver>, with the owner. The asset and the amount received are not stated.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never names USDT as the asset the receiver gets.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);`. The descriptor's redeem fields are only shares/receiver/onBehalf, while mint uses the constant `$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker`. In case 3 the signer received 7199979529 USDT units (7199.98 USDT), and the reader said 'likely USDT-based ... amount not shown'.
findings.fix: Add a field `{label: 'Receive asset', value: '$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker'}` and say 'Redeem {shares} for USDT to {receiver}' in the interpolatedIntent.

findings.title: redeem: the USDT amount received is computed by the vault and has no minimum in calldata.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. In case 3, 7199.979529 USDT arrived, and the screen shows no amount.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show it. It needs a computed field or a min-assets parameter.

cases.notes: The gtusdtf out (7178.31 shares) is shown exactly. The USDT in (7199.98) is not named or quantified, and the reader only guessed the asset.

effects: previewMint(shares) USDT (rounded up) moves from the signer to the vault (enter: safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, ...)). The vault price decides the amount, and no maximum is enforced.
Exactly `shares` gtusdtf are minted to onBehalf.
The deposited USDT may be moved on to the liquidity adapter. That changes no balance of the signer.
formats.shown: Mint 0.000000001 gtusdtf for <onBehalf>. A field names USDT as the deposit asset but gives no amount.

findings.title: mint: the USDT amount taken from the signer is not shown, and calldata gives no maximum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol mint: `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. The descriptor shows only `Deposit asset` = raw constant 'USDT'. In case 1 the signer paid 1 USDT unit, and the screen gives no amount.
findings.fix: No calldata value carries it. It needs a computed field or a max-assets parameter.

findings.title: mint: the intent 'Mint' and its interpolation never say that USDT leaves the signer's wallet.
findings.evidence: descriptor mint: intent 'Mint', interpolatedIntent 'Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'. The code pulls USDT from msg.sender in enter(). In case 1 the reader had to use the separate 'Deposit asset: USDT' field to infer that USDT is spent.
findings.fix: Use intent 'Deposit USDT for shares' and interpolatedIntent 'Deposit USDT to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'.

cases.notes: The USDT out (1 unit) appears only as the asset name with no amount, and the reader knew it had no amount. The shares went to 0xdead (not the signer), and the screen showed this correctly.
